verifications.claim: Artemis 2 reached a peak speed of approximately 25,000 mph (~40,000 km/h) during its re-entry into Earth's atmosphere on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'more than 11 km/s (40,000 km/h) when it reaches Earth's atmosphere... at roughly 8pm April 10'; R2: 'traveling at about 24,000 miles an hour... 7:53 P.M.'; R3: 'peak velocity of 24,664 miles per hour... speeds up to 25,000 mph... April 10, 2026'; R4: '24,661 mph (39688 kph)'; R6: '40,000 kilometers per hour (25,000 miles per hour)'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly confirm the peak re-entry speed around 24,000-25,000 mph / 40,000 km/h specifically for Artemis 2 on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: Approximately 25,000 mph is necessary for the Orion capsule to return from the Moon.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion capsule... travelling at more than 11 km/s (40,000 km/h) when it reaches Earth's atmosphere'; R3: '25,000 mph... for the Orion capsule'; R6: 'Orion reenters... at 40,000 kilometers per hour (25,000 miles per hour)'
verifications.reasoning: References confirm this is the speed Orion reaches on lunar return, implying necessity due to orbital mechanics, but do not explicitly state 'necessary'; broader context supports.

verifications.claim: Artemis 2's peak re-entry speed is more than 30 times the speed of sound.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Orion capsule will re-enter the atmosphere moving at more than 30 times the speed of sound'; R4: '24,661 mph (39688 kph) — Mach 33'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm >30x speed of sound (Mach 33) for Artemis 2 re-entry.

verifications.claim: Artemis 2's peak re-entry speed matches the fastest speeds experienced by humans.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: '25,000 mph... will rival the fastest speed ever experienced by humans'; R4: 'won't break the human spaceflight speed record... 23,840 mph... short of Apollo 10's 24,816 mph... actual 24,661 mph'
verifications.reasoning: References indicate it rivals but does not match or exceed Apollo record (24,816 mph); actual speeds ~24,661 mph are slightly less.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket reached over 17,000 mph during the launch of Artemis 2 to reach orbit.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention SLS rocket speed during Artemis 2 launch; orbital insertion speeds not specified for SLS.

verifications.claim: The spacecraft traveled at approximately 24,527 mph (39,472 km/h) during the translunar injection (TLI) of Artemis 2 to leave Earth's orbit for the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'In the translunar injection (TLI) burn... the spacecraft traveled at 39,472 kilometers (24,527 miles) per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match for speed and event (TLI for Artemis II).

verifications.claim: Orion entered the atmosphere at roughly 24,000 to 25,000 mph during the re-entry of Artemis 2.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'traveling at about 24,000 miles an hour'; R3: 'up to 25,000 mph'; R4: '24,661 mph... hit the atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple direct confirmations of entry speed in 24,000-25,000 mph range for Artemis 2 Orion.

verifications.claim: The capsule slowed to roughly 17 mph during the splashdown of Artemis 2 using a series of parachutes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'at around 17 mph'; R4: 'splashdown at a speed of 17 mph... using parachutes'
verifications.reasoning: Direct matches for final splashdown speed via parachutes.

verifications.claim: During the high-speed re-entry of Artemis 2, the capsule's heat shield protected the crew from temperatures exceeding 10,000°C (over 18,000°F).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'air temperatures of 10,000°C or more... thermal protection system... protects the spacecraft and its crew... pass through air at 10,000°C while maintaining a maximum heat shield surface temperature of only around 3,000°C'
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states external temperatures >10,000°C during re-entry, with heat shield protecting crew; other refs have lower temps but R1 matches exactly.
